reason: Removing losers after seeing outcomes creates selection bias.
violation_example: Dropping DOGEUSDT because C Donchian was negative there.
required_handling: Report all 19 markets and key markets visibly.

reason: Sweeps can fit noise and turn a failed candidate into a backtest artifact.
violation_example: Changing Donchian windows or PF gates after C failed passive BTC.
required_handling: Create a new frozen plan only if explicitly approved and justified by new rationale.

reason: Best relative result may still be weak in absolute and benchmark terms.
violation_example: Promoting C Donchian because it was positive despite passive BTC dominance.
required_handling: Label as fail or caution according to gates.
notes: Positive PnL is not implementation readiness.

reason: Implementation requires evidence of durable edge, not relative ranking among weak candidates.
violation_example: Treating a less negative or mildly positive candidate as ready because others were worse.
required_handling: Keep no-trade default and write postmortem.

reason: A tournament result is first-pass evidence, not operational readiness.
violation_example: Starting dry-run after one candidate clears first-pass gates.
required_handling: Require confirmation plan, confirmation validation, and explicit dry-run approval.
notes: Dry-run and live gates are separate.

reason: Changing data meaning after results creates leakage and provenance errors.
violation_example: Calling aggregate taker-flow exact-instrument flow after a result looks useful.
required_handling: Preserve original data labels and limitations.

reason: Renaming does not create independent evidence.
violation_example: Repackaging Candidate D or funding-gated Candidate D as a new candidate.
required_handling: Reference failed candidates only as context unless a genuinely new approved plan exists.
